title: The Effect of Life Review Intervention on Perception of Aging in Old Women
abstract: Background Aging perception significantly influences mental health in later life, yet effective interventions targeting this multidimensional construct remain underexplored. Aim This randomized controlled trial examined the effect of life review therapy on aging perception among older women. Methods Thirty older women (15 intervention and 15 control) were recruited from comprehensive health centers in Larestan County, Iran. Random allocation was performed using randomized blocks. The intervention group received six weekly 1.5‐hour life review sessions based on Haight and Webster′s protocol; the control group received no intervention. Aging perception was assessed using the validated Persian version of the Aging Perception Questionnaire (APQ) at baseline and postintervention. Between‐group differences were analyzed using independent t ‐tests, and within‐group changes were evaluated with paired t ‐tests. Results Baseline demographic characteristics were comparable between groups ( p > 0.05). In the intervention group, significant improvements were observed in control positive (12.40–14.13, p = 0.015; between‐group p = 0.008) and consequences positive (11.73–13.80, p = 0.009; between‐group p = 0.017). Significant reductions were found in negative emotional representations (17.80–13.07, p = 0.026; between‐group p = 0.013) and negative consequences (29.00–22.60, p = 0.047; between‐group p = 0.010). The control group showed no significant changes across any dimension ( p > 0.05 for all). Conclusion Life review therapy significantly enhanced positive aging perceptions and reduced negative cognitive and emotional responses to aging in older women. This structured, time‐limited intervention offers an effective nonpharmacological strategy for promoting healthy aging and warrants integration into routine geriatric care. Trial Registration: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials: IRCT20250819066915N1
